source.title: Large Stepsize Gradient Descent for Non-Homogeneous Two-Layer Networks: Margin Improvement and Fast Optimization
source.authors: Yu-Hang Cai; Jing-Feng Wu; Song Mei; Michael Lindsey; Peter L. Bartlett

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes and experimentally measures gradient-descent training outcomes in non-convex networks, but its central setting is large-step logistic-loss optimization and margin improvement, not the catalog’s training-error claim as a whole.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-risk and margin results for its own optimization settings. Those results bear on V1 and V5, but do not measure classification training error, corrupted or random labels, or the other claim versions. Figure-only empirical-risk values are not reconstructed. Results cited from other work are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports logistic-loss dynamics and convergence bounds for MLPs and two-layer networks. It does not test V1's convolutional-network training classification error or V5's recovery relative to an identified stability limit, curvature reduction, sharpness tracking, or divergence. Calling the initial oscillations an edge-of-stability phase does not establish those measurements.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The stable-phase and margin results are conditional on reaching a sufficiently low risk. Guaranteed phase transition and acceleration additionally require linear separability and activation conditions, including a derivative bounded away from zero; these guarantees should not be extended to the XOR experiment.
record.recipe_differences: Uses constant-step gradient descent with logistic loss on nearly homogeneous predictors, especially two-layer networks; the claim versions cover several distinct training-error, initialization, depth, stability, and normalization studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper analyzes and compares stepsize choices, showing a change from oscillatory risk early to monotonic decrease after entering the stable phase. Its figures compare multiple stepsizes, but exact values for the two-layer experiments are not stated in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Large-step GD exhibits early logistic-risk oscillation followed by monotonic decrease; larger stepsizes yield smaller risk in the stable phase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large constant stepsizes can produce an oscillatory transient followed by stable logistic-risk convergence in non-homogeneous networks.

fits_no_version.finding: The experiments suggest stable-phase risk scaling as O(1/(η̃t)). Under linear separability and activation assumptions, the theory guarantees eventual stable-phase entry for any constant stepsize and an O(1/T²) terminal-risk bound when the stepsize is chosen for budget T.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitably chosen large stepsizes accelerate logistic-risk optimization in nearly homogeneous two-layer networks under the stated assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized margins nearly monotonically increase in the stable phase, supported by conditional theory and experimental curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stable-phase large-step GD improves normalized margins in nearly homogeneous predictors.

record.problems: Experiments are reported through figures without numerical risk values in the text; the CIFAR-10 experiment uses a two-class subset, and the paper does not report training classification error. The main phase-transition theory requires linearly separable data and an activation derivative bounded away from zero; the XOR experiment is outside that theory.
record.rows_left_out: No reported training-risk experiment is omitted. Margin and test-accuracy curves are not rows for V1 or V5, whose named outcomes are training error and stability-limit loss behavior respectively.

untested.parts: Convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam reaching near-zero classification training error on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; corrupted labels; model-size, stopping, and regularization qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU spurious minima and their dependence on student width.
Depth-related training degradation and comparisons involving residual shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

Squared-loss catapult recovery above an initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, divergence at larger rates, full-batch sharpness tracking at the stability threshold, and divergence from below that threshold.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance comparisons, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels apply to the supplied versions. The absence of numerical figure values is secondary to the mismatch in systems and measured outcomes. Logistic risk approaching zero can imply vanishing classification error, but that does not establish V1 in its named convolutional-network setting. The activation discrepancy for the CIFAR-10 two-layer experiment remains unresolved in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports empirical risk, not training classification error. It does not test CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, or early stopping.
The paper does not compare student and teacher widths or measure spurious local minima.
The paper does not compare plain networks with residual shortcuts or study depth-related training error.
The paper does not compare initialization schemes or measure their effect on trainable depth.

Theoretical analysis and experiments concern large-step gradient descent with logistic loss, not squared-loss wide-network catapult behavior, sharpness at the stability threshold, or runs diverging below that threshold.
The paper does not test batch normalization or Fixup.

rows.subject: multilayer perceptron (MLP) with four trainable layers and GELU activation functions
rows.size_stated: hidden dimension of 200 for each hidden layer
rows.stage_stated: random initialization; trained using gradient descent
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with large stepsize η̃ = 0.2 on the CIFAR-10 subset; empirical risk measured.

conditions.value: 6,000 randomly selected samples from the “airplane” and “automobile” classes of CIFAR-10

rows.baseline: GD with small stepsize η̃ = 0.005; its empirical risk decreases monotonically.
rows.value: The empirical risk oscillates in the first phase but decreases monotonically in the second phase; exact values are figure only.
rows.note: The paper describes the phase pattern but does not state a training classification-error value. Thus this result cannot establish whether training error is near zero.
rows.check: Logistic empirical-risk dynamics in a four-layer MLP do not measure V1's near-zero classification training error in convolutional networks. This is the same experiment recorded in R2.
